## Article

- Citation and DOI: Joel, S., Teper, R., & MacDonald, G. (2014). People overestimate their willingness to reject potential romantic partners by overlooking their concern for other people. *Psychological Science, 25*(12), 2233–2240. DOI: 10.1177/0956797614552828
- Data/materials repository URL: https://osf.io/873fp/
- Part A (known case) or Part B (a classmate's project paper): Part A (known case, `partA_empathy_gap`, Study 1)
- Part B only: the classmate's project repo, and which target outcome is its key effect: Not applicable

## Target outcomes

Written **before** opening the data. Quote each from the paper. In Part B, one of these must
be the project's key effect.

| # | Target outcome (quoted) | Paper value(s) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Only 10 of the 61 participants in the hypothetical condition chose to exchange contact information with the unattractive potential date (16%)." | 10 of 61 (16%) |
| 2 | "In contrast, 26 of the 71 participants in the real condition chose to exchange contact information (37%)." | 26 of 71 (37%) |
| 3 | "A chi-square test of independence indicated that participants were significantly less likely to reject the unattractive potential date in the real condition compared with the hypothetical condition, χ2(1, N = 132) = 6.77, p = .009." | χ²(1, N = 132) = 6.77, p = .009 |

## Reproduction

The agent's work, under your direction. Keep all code visible.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
```

```{r}
#| label: load
d <- read_sav("partA_empathy_gap/data/Empathy Gap Study 1 data.sav")
dim(d)
```

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
# condition: 0 = hypothetical, 1 = real; exchangeinfo: 1 = yes, 2 = no
d1 <- d |>
  transmute(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("hypothetical", "real")),
    exchangeinfo = factor(exchangeinfo, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("yes", "no"))
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(d1))
count(d1, condition, exchangeinfo)
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis
# Target outcomes 1 and 2: descriptives
desc <- d1 |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(n = n(), n_yes = sum(exchangeinfo == "yes"),
            pct_yes = round(100 * n_yes / n, 1))
desc

# Target outcome 3: chi-square test of independence, no continuity correction
tab <- table(d1$condition, d1$exchangeinfo)
chi <- chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)
chi
sprintf("X2(%d, N = %d) = %.2f, p = %.3f", chi$parameter, sum(tab),
        chi$statistic, chi$p.value)
```

## Checker's verdict

Filled in by you, not the agent.

| # | Paper value | Reproduced value | Verdict (exact / minor / major / not reproducible) | Reason for discrepancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 of 61 (16%) | 10 of 61 (16%)  |exact | None |
| 2 | 26 of 71 (37%) | 26 of 71 (37%) |exact |None |
| 3 | χ²(1, N = 132) = 6.77, p = .009 |  χ²(1, N = 132) = 6.77, p = .009 |exact |None |

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right:

Claude said it finished writing the report and calculated three values in Python (10 out of 61, 26 out of 71, and χ² = 6.77). Claude also said it still needed to run the R code and render the report. I rendered the report myself, and this ran the R code. Then I compared the results with the article. All three values matched, so I concluded that the results were reproduced.

- Your time (hours): 0.58 (35 minutes)

- Stopped at the 4-hour cap? What remained: No.

## Assessment

Is the primary result analytically reproducible? What would have made this take 30 minutes?

Yes. I rendered the report, which ran the R code, and got the same three values as in the article (10 out of 61, 26 out of 71, and χ² = 6.77). I think I could have finished in 30 minutes if I had connected the correct folder from the start.
